contentSections: Every year the same thing happens. Relatives arrive, the street fills with lights, and your house gets judged in about four seconds from the gate. If the front wall still looks like it did in 2019, no amount of rangoli will hide it.

Most families answer this with fresh paint. It is the cheapest option, and it works for a few months. But if you want a Diwali home exterior makeover that still looks sharp next Diwali and the one after, paint is the wrong tool. A proper house facade upgrade changes the material, the light and the depth of the front elevation, and that is what people actually notice.

This guide covers seven upgrades that work on Indian homes, what each one costs roughly, how long it takes, and how to pick a facade company that will not leave your scaffolding standing through the festival.
Quick Answer: What Should You Upgrade Before Diwali?

If you only have budget or time for one change, pick a metal accent wall on the main elevation and light it properly. If you have room for two, add a wood finish aluminium porch ceiling or a laser cut screen on the balcony.

• Best for visual impact: metal accent cladding (fluted, coin or cassette panels)
  • Best for warmth: wood finish aluminium on porch and soffit
  • Best for privacy plus style: laser cut jaali screens
  • Best for night views: planned LED grazing and warm white wall washers
  • Best for budget: a canopy and a louvered gate instead of a full elevation change
Why a Diwali Home Exterior Makeover Needs More Than a Coat of Paint

Paint sits on the surface. Dust, monsoon humidity and summer sun attack it every year, so the colour that looked rich in October looks tired by the next rainy season. You also repeat the cost and the scaffolding every few years.
A facade upgrade is different in three ways.

First, it adds depth. A flat plastered wall catches light evenly and looks flat. A fluted or textured metal panel throws shadows that change from morning to evening, so the house looks different at different times of day.

Second, it adds permanence. Powder coated or PVDF coated aluminium does not need repainting. At Metaguise, our coating systems carry 15 to 30 year warranties depending on the finish, which is why we push clients away from repeat painting and towards a one time upgrade.
Third, it adds resale and rental value. A front elevation makeover is one of the few renovations a buyer can see from the road before even entering the house.
If you are still deciding between repainting and a full redesign, our guide to house exterior design in India and the 10 materials that last 30 years helps you compare options before you call anyone.
7 Facade Upgrades for a Diwali Home Exterior Makeover
1. A Metal Accent Wall on the Main Elevation
You do not need to clad the whole house. Pick the one wall your eye lands on first, usually the wall around the main door or the double height portion of the staircase, and cover it in metal.

A 150 sq ft accent wall is enough to change the character of a bungalow or builder floor. Fluted panels give a clean vertical rhythm. Coin or circular modules give a jewellery-like shimmer. Flat cassette panels give a sharp, minimal look.
Good options to explore are MetaFlute vertical fluted panels, MetaCassette flat wall panels and the MetaCoin circular module.
2. Fluted Panels Around the Entrance
The entrance is where guests pause. A fluted metal surround, even just a three foot band either side of the door, gives that pause a focal point.

Fluted profiles also hide small surface flaws better than flat panels, which is useful if your wall is not perfectly even. They work in gold, bronze, graphite and wood tones, so they sit comfortably with both traditional and contemporary homes.
3. Wood Finish Aluminium for Porch and Soffit
Many Indian homeowners love the warmth of timber but have been burned by it. Termites, warping in monsoon, and yearly polishing are real costs.

Wood finish aluminium gives you the grain and colour of timber without those problems. It is a strong choice for porch ceilings, pergola fascia and the soffit above your entrance. Look at MetaWood if you want this look on a facade rather than just indoors.
4. Laser Cut Jaali Screens for Balconies and Gates

Jaali is not new to India, but laser cut metal makes it far more precise. A screen with a geometric or floral pattern can hide a washing area, soften the afternoon sun and light up beautifully after dark.

Pattern choice matters. Dense patterns give privacy but cut airflow. Open patterns breathe but show more. If you want to understand how open area changes the result, read our breakdown of laser cut metal facade panels and their real challenges.
5. A Canopy That Frames the Door
A canopy does two jobs. It shields the door from rain and sun, and it gives the elevation a strong horizontal line, which makes narrow houses look wider.
Corten finish canopies develop a rich rust tone. Powder coated aluminium canopies stay crisp in black, white or champagne. For a fuller view of materials, see MetaCorten.
6. A Louvered Gate and Boundary Upgrade
Your gate is part of the facade, whether you planned it or not. A tired iron gate under a freshly cladded wall looks like a mismatch.
Metal louvers keep privacy, allow air, and can match the colour of your cladding. Browse MetaLouver for options, or read our ideas on louvered gate design for Indian homes.
7. Lighting That Is Planned, Not Strung
Diwali lights are temporary. Architectural lighting stays all year.

The simple rules: use warm white between 2700K and 3000K so metal looks rich rather than clinical; graze light along textured panels from above or below to show depth; keep fixtures IP65 rated or better for outdoor use; and hide the source so people see the glow, not the bulb.
Plan the lighting with the cladding. Cable routes and fixture pockets are far easier to build in than to retrofit.

Over ten years, repeated painting plus scaffolding often costs more than people expect, which is why the upgrade usually wins on lifetime cost even though the first bill is bigger.
How Much Does a House Facade Upgrade Cost in India?

Cost depends on the system, the complexity of the design and the access to your site. As an indicative range, installed metal facade systems from Metaguise fall between roughly INR 800 and INR 2,500 per sq ft.
So a 150 sq ft accent wall could land between INR 1.2 lakh and INR 3.75 lakh. A simple louvered gate or canopy will usually sit below that. A full custom parametric elevation will sit above.
What moves the price up or down:

• Panel type: flat cassette is cheaper than a custom 3D module
  • Finish: standard powder coat is cheaper than PVDF or specialty patina
  • Height: anything needing heavy scaffolding or a crane costs more to install
  • Custom patterns: anything that needs new tooling costs more than a catalogue profile
  • Lighting integration: built in channels add labour but save rework
For a deeper breakdown, our metal facade cost guide for India lists rates by system and project type.
How Long Does It Take? Plan Backwards From Diwali
This is where most festive makeovers fail. People call a contractor three weeks before Diwali and discover that fabrication alone takes longer than that.
A realistic sequence looks like this:

1. Site visit and measurement
  2. Design and your approval
  3. Fabrication of panels and sub-frame
  4. Coating and quality check
  5. Installation
  6. Lighting and final cleaning

Small accent projects are quicker than full elevations, but none of this happens overnight. If Diwali is close, ask your facade company honestly what can be finished safely and what should wait. A half-finished elevation during the festival is worse than an old one.
The smarter move is to do the structural and cladding work now, and plan the lighting upgrade as phase two if time runs short.
5 Mistakes That Ruin a Festive Exterior Makeover
Cladding over a damp wall. If water is seeping through, panels will hide the problem for a while and then fail. Fix waterproofing first.
Choosing colour from a phone screen. Metal finishes shift with light. Always see a physical sample outdoors, at morning and evening, before approving.
Ignoring the sub-frame. The visible panel gets all the attention, but the frame behind it decides how the facade holds up in wind and heat.
Buying from a trader instead of a maker. If the seller cannot show you the fabrication process, you cannot hold anyone accountable for tolerances or finish.
Forgetting maintenance access. Think about how the wall will be washed and where the ladder or rope access will go before panels go up.
How to Choose a Facade Company for a Home Exterior Renovation
Not every facade company handles homes well. Some are built for towers and treat a bungalow as a small job. Others are decorators who buy panels from somewhere and fit them.
Ask these questions:

• Do you design, fabricate and install, or do you outsource part of it?
  • Can I see completed homes, and can I speak to those owners?
  • What coating warranty do you give in writing?
  • Will you make a sample or mock-up before full production?
  • Who is on site during installation?

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the best facade upgrade for Diwali?
A metal accent wall around the main entrance gives the biggest visual change for the money. Add warm white lighting to it and the house looks transformed both by day and during Diwali evenings.

How early should I start a house facade upgrade before Diwali?
Start at least two to three months ahead. Design approval, fabrication, coating and installation each take time, and rushing any of them risks poor finish quality or a half-finished elevation during the festival.

Is metal cladding better than paint for a house exterior?
For long term value, yes. Coated metal holds its colour for years and needs only washing, while paint needs repeating every few years. Paint is cheaper at the start, but metal usually costs less over a decade.

Can I upgrade only one part of my house front?
Yes. Many homeowners start with an accent wall, an entrance surround or a canopy. A good facade company will design the first phase so more sections can be added later without mismatched finishes.

How much does a front elevation makeover cost in India?
Installed metal facade systems from Metaguise typically fall between INR 800 and INR 2,500 per sq ft, depending on the system and complexity. A small accent wall costs far less than a full elevation.

Will metal cladding get too hot in an Indian summer?
Light and mid-tone coated finishes manage heat well, and a ventilated sub-frame lets hot air escape behind the panels. Very dark colours on west-facing walls need extra care, so ask your supplier for guidance.
